name: Balboa and Cristóbal container ports (Panama Ports Company)
value: Run since 1997 by Panama Ports Company, a CK Hutchison unit; extended in 2021 to 2047; the 2025 sale to a BlackRock and MSC group (part of a $22.8bn, 43-port deal) stalled when COSCO sought a stake; Panama's Supreme Court voided the contract on 29 Jan 2026 and the state took the ports in Feb 2026
lender_builder: CK Hutchison (Hong Kong conglomerate); COSCO Shipping sought a stake in the 2025 sale
china_gets: Until 2026, a Hong Kong group's control of the container terminals at both ends of the Panama Canal; in the 2025 sale talks Beijing pressed for COSCO, a Chinese state shipping line, to get a share
host_position: Panama's comptroller found unpaid fees and a 2021 extension that was never approved; the court ruled the deal unconstitutional and Maersk now runs the ports on an interim basis; Hutchison denies wrongdoing
confidence_reason: The operator is a private Hong Kong company, not a Chinese state firm; the court ruling and seizure are documented

name: Fourth bridge over the Panama Canal
value: $1.42bn design-and-build contract awarded in 2018; road and metro-rail crossing
lender_builder: Panama Cuarto Puente consortium of China Communications Construction (CCCC) and China Harbour Engineering (CHEC), both Chinese state firms
china_gets: A flagship construction contract on the canal itself for Chinese state builders
host_position: Panama says the bridge relieves traffic between Panama City and the western suburbs and carries Metro Line 3
confidence_reason: The award is documented; later delays and changes to the timetable are not fully confirmed in the sources

name: Panama City-David railway (cancelled)
value: Chinese feasibility study delivered in March 2019: 391km, about $4.1bn; shelved by the Cortizo government in September 2019
lender_builder: China Railway Design Corporation (study, paid for by China)
china_gets: Would have been a large railway-building contract; nothing was built
host_position: President Varela backed it after Panama recognised Beijing in 2017; his successor Cortizo dropped it
confidence_reason: Study and cancellation reported by Panamanian media

name: North-South Highway (Edward Seaga Highway)
value: About $730m; 66km toll road opened 2016; China Development Bank loans of $425.5m plus RMB 200m (Libor+4.6%, 20 years)
lender_builder: China Harbour Engineering (CHEC) through its project company; China Development Bank
china_gets: A 50-year toll concession and the right to up to 1,200 acres of state land along the route
host_position: Jamaica gave no loan or traffic guarantees and says the road cut the Kingston-Ocho Rios trip to under an hour; tolls are criticised as high
confidence_reason: Terms from Jamaica's government information service and AidData

name: Alpart alumina refinery and bauxite lands
value: Bought from Rusal for $299m in 2016, helped by a $170m China Development Bank loan
lender_builder: JISCO (Jiuquan Iron and Steel, a Chinese state steel and aluminium group)
china_gets: A bauxite and alumina source for Chinese aluminium production
host_position: Jamaica welcomed the restart of an idle plant and jobs in the south-west
confidence_reason: Sale confirmed by Rusal; loan by AidData

name: Route 32 widening, San José to Limón
value: $296m China Exim loan signed in 2013 (4%, 20 years); the loan ran out in April 2025 and Costa Rica is finishing the work itself
lender_builder: China Exim Bank; China Harbour Engineering (CHEC) builds it
china_gets: A building contract on the road to Costa Rica's main Caribbean port
host_position: Costa Rica says the road is vital for exports through Limón; delays and cost overruns are a domestic issue
confidence_reason: Loan terms from AidData and Costa Rica's public works ministry

name: National Stadium, San José
value: About $105m Chinese grant; opened 2011
lender_builder: Chinese government grant; built by a Chinese state firm
china_gets: A visible reward after Costa Rica switched recognition from Taiwan to Beijing in 2007
host_position: Costa Rica got a national stadium at no cost
confidence_reason: Grant recorded by AidData

name: Moín oil refinery joint venture (cancelled)
value: $1.3bn upgrade planned through Soresco, a 50-50 venture of state oil firm Recope and CNPC; halted in 2013 and cancelled in 2016
lender_builder: CNPC (China National Petroleum Corporation) and China Development Bank financing
china_gets: Would have given a Chinese state oil firm half of Costa Rica's only refinery; nothing was built
host_position: Costa Rica's comptroller found a conflict of interest because the feasibility study was done by a CNPC subsidiary
confidence_reason: Halt and cancellation reported by Reuters and the Tico Times

name: Baha Mar resort, Nassau
value: $2.45bn China Exim loan (2010; Libor+3.9%); bankruptcy in 2015; sold by the bank's holding vehicle to Hong Kong's Chow Tai Fook Enterprises in 2017
lender_builder: China Exim Bank; China State Construction Engineering (CSCEC) built it and put in $150m
china_gets: Interest income and a huge contract for a Chinese state builder; the bank took control of the resort after the collapse
host_position: The Bahamas backed the project as a jobs engine; the developer blamed the Chinese builder for delays
confidence_reason: Loan terms from AidData and the loan documents; the sale reported by PR Newswire and the Tribune

name: North Abaco port
value: About $40m China Exim loan (2%, 20 years) for the port and a bridge; handed over in 2018
lender_builder: China Exim Bank; China Harbour Engineering (CHEC) built it
china_gets: A building contract about 200 miles from Florida; no Chinese operating rights
host_position: The Bahamas wanted a second port for Abaco; it is still mostly unused for commercial shipping
confidence_reason: Loan and contract announced by the Bahamas government; use reported by the Tribune

name: Suspected Chinese-linked listening stations (Bejucal and El Salao)
value: No figures; satellite images show active antennas at Bejucal near Havana and a large antenna ring under construction at El Salao near Guantanamo since 2021; work at El Salao stopped by April 2025
lender_builder: Cuban military with suspected Chinese involvement (reported)
china_gets: Possible electronic eavesdropping on US military and space activity in the south-eastern US
host_position: Cuba and China deny any Chinese spy base
confidence_reason: Based on CSIS satellite analysis and anonymous US officials; China's role is not confirmed

name: Santiago de Cuba multipurpose terminal
value: $120m China Exim loan; built 2015-2018, opened January 2019
lender_builder: China Exim Bank; China Communications Construction (CCCC)
china_gets: A building contract and a creditor role in Cuba's second port
host_position: Cuba says the terminal modernises trade for the east of the island
confidence_reason: Loan recorded by AidData; opening reported by Cuban media

name: Chinese-supplied solar parks
value: 92 parks planned, 55 in 2025, aiming at more than 2,000 megawatts by 2028; China donated equipment for 22 parks (120 megawatts) in 2025
lender_builder: Chinese state equipment makers, including Shanghai Electric; Chinese government donation
china_gets: Influence as Cuba's main helper in its power crisis, taking Russia's place
host_position: Cuba says the parks are its fastest way to end blackouts
confidence_reason: Reported by Reuters with figures from Cuba's energy ministry

name: St John's deep-water harbour
value: About $90m; RMB 600m China Exim concessional loan (2%, matures 2038); finished 2020
lender_builder: China Exim Bank; China Civil Engineering Construction (CCECC)
china_gets: A building contract and creditor role in the main port of a small island state
host_position: Antigua says the port lets bigger cruise and cargo ships call
confidence_reason: Loan terms from AidData; completion reported locally

name: Phoenix Park industrial estate, Point Lisas
value: Opened January 2024; financed by China Exim Bank and built by Beijing Construction Engineering Group (BCEG)
lender_builder: China Exim Bank; BCEG (a Beijing state builder)
china_gets: A Caribbean manufacturing base where Chinese firms lease space
host_position: Trinidad wants the estate to draw manufacturing and diversify from oil and gas
confidence_reason: Opening confirmed by Trinidad's trade ministry; loan size not published

name: Sam Lord's Castle hotel
value: $170m China Exim buyer's credit; opened as a Wyndham Grand hotel in October 2023
lender_builder: China Exim Bank; COMPLANT (a Chinese state builder) built it
china_gets: A building contract and interest income
host_position: Barbados backed the rebuilt resort for tourism jobs; local builders complained of being pushed out
confidence_reason: Loan recorded by AidData; opening by Wyndham

name: New Demerara River Bridge
value: $260.85m contract signed 2022; opened October 2025; paid for by Guyana
lender_builder: China Railway Construction Corporation (CRCC) group
china_gets: A large building contract in a fast-growing oil economy
host_position: Guyana says the four-lane bridge ends chronic traffic on the old floating bridge
confidence_reason: Contract and opening confirmed by Guyana's information department

name: Nicaragua canal concession (revoked)
value: Granted in 2013 to HKND, a Hong Kong company owned by businessman Wang Jing; nothing beyond a symbolic start was built; repealed in May 2024
lender_builder: HKND Group (private, Hong Kong)
china_gets: Would have given a Chinese businessman a 50-year (renewable) right to build a rival to the Panama Canal
host_position: Ortega's government revoked the concession and says it will seek other investors; farmers had protested land seizures
confidence_reason: Repeal published in Nicaragua's official gazette and reported by AP

name: Punta Huete international airport rebuild
value: RMB 2.87bn (about $400m) credit from CAMCE approved in 2024 (15 years, about 5.2%), after Nicaragua switched recognition from Taiwan to Beijing in 2021
lender_builder: China CAMC Engineering (CAMCE), a Chinese state firm, as lender and builder
china_gets: A building contract and creditor role at a former military airfield near Managua
host_position: Nicaragua says the airport will be a new international gateway
confidence_reason: Loan terms in Nicaragua's legislative decree and AidData

name: National Library and La Libertad tourist pier
value: National Library opened November 2023 (about $54m, mostly Chinese); La Libertad pier, about $23m Chinese grant, opened 2024
lender_builder: Chinese government grants
china_gets: Visible goodwill after El Salvador switched recognition from Taiwan to Beijing in 2018
host_position: President Bukele presents both as Chinese gifts with no strings
confidence_reason: Opening reported by AP; pier grant recorded by AidData

name: Patuca III hydropower dam
value: 104 megawatts; opened January 2021; phase 2 financed by a $297.7m ICBC loan
lender_builder: Sinohydro (PowerChina); ICBC (a Chinese state bank)
china_gets: A dam contract won before Honduras switched recognition from Taiwan to Beijing in 2023
host_position: Honduras says the dam cuts reliance on imported fuel for power
confidence_reason: Loan recorded by AidData
